description: Kalshi fee parameters, versioned by EFFECTIVE TIME. A recommendation is priced with the schedule in force at its decision timestamp, never with whatever happens to be current when the importer runs twelve hours later.

source_hierarchy.what: The Kalshi Fee Schedule filed with the CFTC. Lists BOTH a Maker Multiplier and a Taker Multiplier per non-standard series.
source_hierarchy.why_first: It is the published, dated, regulatory instrument. It is the only source that carries the maker multiplier at all.

source_hierarchy.why_second: Live and machine-readable, but fee_multiplier is the TAKER multiplier only -- the object carries no separate maker parameter. Its silence about maker is not evidence that the maker multiplier is unknown.

source_hierarchy.why_third: Forward-looking. Used to build the NEXT schedule window, not to override the one in force.

conflict_policy: FAIL_CLOSED. Where two sources disagree about a series' multiplier for the same effective window, the fee state for that series is CONFLICTED, net EV cannot be computed, and a RECOMMENDED record on it is refused. A conflict is reported, never silently resolved by rank.

verification_policy.check_cadence: weekly, via the fee-health job in .github/workflows/kalshi-fee-health.yml
verification_policy.why_this_cadence: Fee schedules change on the order of once or twice a year and are announced in advance through GET /series/fee_changes, so a ten-minute cadence would buy nothing. A weekly check against a 45-day tolerance means three consecutive missed checks before real recommendations block -- enough slack for a broken runner, not enough for a months-old unchecked registry to price real money.
verification_policy.on_change: CAPTURE, SURFACE, BLOCK, REVIEW. An observed difference or an announced change is written to the append-only fee observations on market-data, fails the health job loudly, blocks affected real recommendations through the fee_schedule_established gate, and requires a reviewed edit to this file adding a NEW effective window. Nothing auto-edits this file: an API response must never silently rewrite the schedule that every historical net-EV number in the ledger was computed against.
verification_policy.historical_windows: Existing windows are never modified or removed. A change adds a window with its own effective_from and closes the previous window's effective_to, so a past decision keeps being priced with the schedule that was actually in force when it was made.

contract_granularity.what_this_controls: The worst-case fill count in nfl_edge/execution/fees.rounding_uncertainty, which bounds how much more a fragmented order can cost than the same order in one fill per price level.
contract_granularity.why_unknown_is_the_default: Kalshi order sizes are fixed-point with a documented 0.01-contract minimum increment, and fills of 0.30 or 0.03 contracts are ordinary. A whole-dollar approved stake buys a FRACTIONAL number of contracts ($10 at 0.62 is 16.13), so nothing about our own sizing implies whole-contract fills. UNKNOWN is priced identically to FRACTIONAL_ENABLED: 'we could not establish that fractional trading is disabled' may never shrink a cost bound.
contract_granularity.how_to_set_a_series_to_whole_contracts: Only with venue metadata that PROVES fractional trading is disabled for that series. Add it under `series` as {"KXWHATEVER": {"state": "WHOLE_CONTRACTS_ONLY", "evidence": "...", "verified_at": "YYYY-MM-DD"}} in a reviewed commit, exactly as a fee multiplier is recorded. Never infer it from a silent API object.

rounding.notes: The trade fee is ceiled to a CENTICENT ($0.0001). The resulting balance change is then floored to the account's balance precision, and the difference is charged as a ROUNDING FEE. That overpayment accumulates per order across all of its fills, taker and maker alike; once the accumulator exceeds one cent a whole-cent REBATE is issued and the accumulator is reduced by a cent. Net fee = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate, never below zero. The accumulator is what makes many small fills converge to the cost of one equivalent fill.

schedules.verification_note: The session that wrote this file could not reach kalshi.com or the Kalshi API (network egress policy), so the per-series multipliers below are recorded from the operator's reading of the July 2026 regulatory Fee Schedule and are marked with the evidence that supports each one. scripts/kalshi/capture_fee_metadata.py re-reads the live API from GitHub Actions and reports any disagreement.
schedules.default_note: The published schedule states the maker multiplier is 0 unless a series is listed otherwise. That default applies ONLY to series whose captured fee_type is 'quadratic' (taker-only). A series whose fee_type is 'quadratic_with_maker_fees' charges a maker fee by construction, so a 0 default would be plainly wrong for it -- such a series must be listed below or its maker multiplier is UNVERIFIED.
schedules.settlement_note: Kalshi does not currently charge a separate settlement fee on these markets. Recorded explicitly so the assumption is visible and testable rather than implicit in a missing term.
